items.name: component-top-nav-mega-menu-item
items.title: Top Nav Mega Menu Item
items.description: An individual item inside an TopNavMegaMenu. Renders itself in both desktop (popover grid) and mobile drawer modes via render mode context.
items.author: Astryx

items.name: component-top-nav-menu
items.title: Top Nav Menu
items.description: Navigation item that displays a hover-triggered popover menu with rich items containing an icon, title, and optional description.
items.author: Astryx

items.name: component-tree-list
items.title: Tree List
items.description: Tree list container. Accepts items data and rendering configuration. Expansion state is managed internally.
items.author: Astryx

items.name: component-typeahead
items.title: Typeahead
items.description: Styled typeahead with label, description, validation, and all field features. Wraps BaseTypeahead with Field for the primary use case.
items.author: Astryx

items.name: component-typeahead-item
items.title: Typeahead Item
items.description: Default dropdown item renderer for typeahead results. Shows label with optional icon, description, and avatar. Exported for use in custom renderItem implementations.
items.author: Astryx

items.name: component-v-stack
items.title: V Stack
items.description: Vertical stack for arranging items top-to-bottom. Supports polymorphic rendering.
items.author: Astryx

items.name: component-visually-hidden
items.title: VisuallyHidden
items.description: Renders content in the accessibility tree while hiding it visually. Use for accessible names on icon-only controls, aria-live announcement regions, and supplementary screen-reader context. Deliberately has no styling props; the whole point is to stay invisible.
items.author: Astryx

items.name: hook-use-announce
items.title: useAnnounce
items.description: Imperatively announces a message to screen readers through a visually-hidden live region. Use it for state that is only conveyed visually; search result counts, "no results", loading and saved confirmations, validation errors (WCAG 4.1.3 Status Messages). The polite and assertive regions are created empty on first use and stay mounted, which is what makes announcements reliable: most screen readers ignore a live region that is inserted together with its content. Each message is cleared a couple of seconds after it is announced so stale status does not linger in the accessibility tree.
items.author: Astryx

items.name: hook-use-app-shell-mobile
items.title: useAppShellMobile
items.description: Hook for reading and controlling AppShell mobile navigation state from descendants of AppShell. Use it for custom mobile nav triggers, closing the drawer after route changes, or coordinating AppShell-adjacent mobile experiences with the same breakpoint used by mobile nav.
items.author: Astryx

items.name: hook-use-clickable-container
items.title: useClickableContainer
items.description: Makes a container element clickable while preserving nested interactive element behavior. Solves the "nested interactive elements" problem: when a card is clickable but contains buttons/links, clicking those should NOT trigger the card's action. Detects interactive ancestors between the click target and the container, and ignores text selections. Supports href navigation (including middle-click and Ctrl/Cmd+click for new tabs).
items.author: Astryx

items.name: hook-use-clipboard
items.title: useClipboard
items.description: Copy-to-clipboard behavior: the clipboard write, a transient isCopied flag with its own reset timer, and an optional polite screen-reader announcement. Extracted so every copy affordance is a thin control over one implementation instead of re-deriving the timer and announcement. Rapid re-copies restart the reset timer so the confirmation always lasts the full duration, and the timer is cleaned up on unmount. CodeBlock and Timestamp build their built-in copy buttons on it; reach for it directly when building a copy affordance that is not a plain icon button (a menu item, a labeled text button, a copy-on-click value chip).
items.author: Astryx

items.name: hook-use-collapsible
items.title: useCollapsible
items.description: Reusable hook that encapsulates the collapsible state machine. Supports three modes: group-controlled (inside CollapsibleGroup), controlled (isOpen + onOpenChange), and uncontrolled (self-managed with defaultIsOpen). Used internally by Card and Section.
items.author: Astryx

items.name: hook-use-collator
items.title: useCollator
items.description: Returns the sanctioned locale-aware comparator for custom sorting. The collator is recreated when the provider locale or an option changes.
items.author: Astryx

items.name: hook-use-combobox
items.title: useCombobox
items.description: Tracks the active option of a single-select combobox and handles its keys, while DOM focus stays on the control. It powers Selector and CommandPalette; use it to build a combobox those components do not cover. It renders nothing and sets no attributes: the caller renders the control, the listbox and the options, and wires `role`, `aria-expanded`, `aria-controls` and `aria-activedescendant` from what it returns.
items.author: Astryx

items.name: hook-use-container-reveal
items.title: useContainerReveal
items.description: A headless hover/focus reveal primitive. Gives a container a scoped trigger that reveals (or conceals) content inside it when the container is hovered or receives keyboard focus: the classic "row actions appear on hover" pattern. The reveal is CSS-only: no hover state lives in React and hovering never triggers a re-render. The caller authors no StyleX for the reveal itself; the hook hands out the container and content styles, and a nested container shadows its ancestor, so nested containers never leak hover/focus into one another. Accessible by construction: revealed content is visually hidden at rest with position and opacity (never display:none), so it stays mounted, keeps its place in the tab order, and is announced to assistive technology; it reveals on :focus-within so keyboard users see it when tabbing in, stays visible on touch (never gated behind hover on coarse pointers), and honors prefers-reduced-motion.
items.author: Astryx

items.name: hook-use-dev-warning
items.title: useDevWarning
items.description: Fires a dev-only "Component: message" console warning once per mount while the condition holds. It is the render-safe way for a component to flag misuse: warning straight from the render body repeats on every render, and gating it with state adds a re-render, so this uses a ref and an effect instead. For a warning outside a component, use the imperative devWarn utility.
items.author: Astryx

items.name: hook-use-entry-animation
items.title: useEntryAnimation
items.description: Returns a StyleX style for animating an element on mount. Only animates when the element is dynamically inserted after the initial page paint; elements rendered on page load are not animated. Uses Astryx motion tokens (duration, easing) for consistent animation timing. Server-rendered elements hydrate without the entry style and never animate; elements mounted after hydration animate.
items.author: Astryx

items.name: hook-use-focus-trap
items.title: useFocusTrap
items.description: Traps focus within a container element following the WAI-ARIA dialog focus trap pattern. Listens to focus events on the document and redirects focus back into the container if it escapes via keyboard navigation. Handles both Tab and Shift+Tab wrapping. When the trap deactivates or unmounts, focus is restored to the element that was focused before activation, unless focus was already moved elsewhere or never entered the trap (so popups that keep focus on their trigger, like comboboxes, are unaffected). Mouse clicks outside the container are not intercepted; use a light-dismiss handler for that.
items.author: Astryx

items.name: hook-use-grid-focus
items.title: useGridFocus
items.description: Manages keyboard navigation within a 2D grid following the WAI-ARIA grid pattern. Supports arrow keys for cell-to-cell navigation, Home/End for row boundaries, Ctrl+Home/Ctrl+End for grid boundaries, and Page Up/Down for custom callbacks (e.g., month navigation in calendars). Boundary navigation callbacks allow cross-grid navigation.
items.author: Astryx

items.name: hook-use-hotkeys
items.title: useHotkeys
items.description: Registers global keyboard shortcuts with a single window keydown listener per hook instance. Handlers live in a ref, so re-renders never re-subscribe. Skips events from typing targets (input, textarea, select, contenteditable) unless allowInInputs, skips defaultPrevented events, and calls preventDefault() on match. SSR-safe.
items.author: Astryx

items.name: hook-use-hover-card
items.title: useHoverCard
items.description: Headless hook for hover-triggered floating cards. Builds on useLayer with hover/focus intent detection, configurable delays, safe hover behavior, and accessible aria-describedby linking. Use for rich previews on hover when you need full control over the trigger or rendered content.
items.author: Astryx

items.name: hook-use-image-mode
items.title: useImageMode
items.description: Detects whether an image is predominantly dark or light by sampling pixels via OffscreenCanvas. Uses APCA perceptual lightness (sRGB linearization + power curve) for accurate detection, especially on saturated colors. Runs entirely off the paint path: no visible canvas, no layout thrash. Supports regional sampling for detecting luminance where text overlays will appear. Returns null while loading and falls back gracefully on CORS or network errors.
items.author: Astryx

items.name: hook-use-imperative-alert-dialog
items.title: useImperativeAlertDialog
items.description: Hook for showing an alert dialog without managing open state. Call alert.show(options) to open and alert.hide() to close. Render alert.element in your JSX tree.
items.author: Astryx

items.name: hook-use-imperative-dialog
items.title: useImperativeDialog
items.description: Hook for showing a dialog without managing open state. Call dialog.show(content, options) to open and dialog.hide() to close. Render dialog.element in your JSX tree.
items.author: Astryx

items.name: hook-use-indicator-focus-ring
items.title: useIndicatorFocusRing
items.description: Draws the standard focus ring on the indicator of a control whose real input is visually hidden; a checkbox or radio focuses an opacity-0 input, so the ring has to appear on the picture beside it. The ring is painted imperatively on the indicator's own element, which is the only element whose border-radius can shape it, and only on :focus-visible, so pointer clicks stay quiet. Owning it here means a theme-supplied indicator cannot ship a control with no visible focus (WCAG 2.4.7) by ignoring a prop.
items.author: Astryx

items.name: hook-use-input-container
items.title: useInputContainer
items.description: Makes an input container wrapper clickable, delegating focus to the inner input/textarea when the user clicks non-interactive areas (icons, padding, status indicators). Built on top of useClickableContainer, so nested interactive elements (clear buttons, calendar toggles, links) are handled safely; clicking them does NOT steal focus from the input. Automatically detects input type: text-like inputs receive .focus(), while other types (checkbox, radio, file) receive .click().
items.author: Astryx

items.name: hook-use-input-status-icon
items.title: useInputStatusIcon
items.description: Builds the on-field status affordance for a bordered input and its accessibility wiring, so every input in the family behaves the same for a given status. The attached variant renders a plain glyph and leaves the text to the message box; the detached variant renders nothing here, because the message box already carries its own icon; the tooltip variant renders a real focusable button whose tooltip is reachable by keyboard, pointer, touch and assistive tech. Use it when building a bordered input, not for field-level messaging.
items.author: Astryx

items.name: hook-use-interactive-role
items.title: useInteractiveRole
items.description: Resolves what a polymorphic component should render as, in one place: href wins, then onClick, then an interactive trigger context supplied by a parent (Popover, DropdownMenu and friends), then inert. Use it in any component that is sometimes a link, sometimes a button, and sometimes plain content; Token, Thumbnail, Item and ClickableCard all do. Because context is part of the resolution, a component built on it becomes a valid trigger for new surfaces without changing.
items.author: Astryx

items.name: hook-use-keyboard-hint
items.title: useKeyboardHint
items.description: Shows an ephemeral "← → to navigate" hint anchored to the focused item the first time a roving-tabindex composite (Toolbar, TabList, SegmentedControl, etc.) receives keyboard focus. It teaches sighted keyboard users that arrow keys move within the group. The hint renders arrow keys with Kbd in the top layer (popover="manual") and is CSS-anchor-positioned to the focused element, so overflow containers never clip it. It auto-dismisses on the first arrow press, on timeout, or on blur, and does not re-show for that instance. Toolbar, TabList, and SegmentedControl wire this in automatically; reach for the hook directly only when building a custom roving-tabindex widget.
items.author: Astryx

items.name: hook-use-layer
items.title: useLayer
items.description: Core positioning hook for rendering overlay content using CSS Anchor Positioning and the Popover API. Use it as the foundation for custom popovers, hover cards, tooltips, and fixed-position layers when higher-level components are not enough. Both modes use theme body text defaults and end ancestor surface/group membership as a whole, including group-owned state. Explicit props and unrelated contexts remain unchanged. Apply intentional formatting through render styles or content, and establish complete content-local providers inside the rendered layer.
items.author: Astryx

items.name: hook-use-list-focus
items.title: useListFocus
items.description: Manages keyboard navigation within a linear list following WAI-ARIA menu/listbox/toolbar patterns. Supports arrow key navigation (vertical, horizontal, or both), Home/End for boundaries, optional wrap-around, RTL, and Escape to close. Opt into hasRovingTabIndex for composite widgets (toolbars, segmented controls, tab strips) that own a single tab stop. Suitable for dropdown menus, toolbars, and any 1D focusable list.
items.author: Astryx

items.name: hook-use-locale
items.title: useLocale
items.description: Reads the authoritative Astryx locale. Use it to thread the provider locale into pure formatting helpers and sibling-package APIs; do not derive a second locale from navigator.language or a hardcoded literal.
items.author: Astryx

items.name: hook-use-long-press
items.title: useLongPress
items.description: Detects a single-finger press-and-hold and reports where it happened, so touch users can reach affordances that a pointer gets from right-click. iOS Safari never synthesizes a contextmenu event on long-press, which makes this the only touch route into a cursor-positioned surface such as ContextMenu. The press cancels on movement, lift, multi-touch or unmount.
items.author: Astryx

items.name: hook-use-media-query
items.title: useMediaQuery
items.description: SSR-safe media query hook that subscribes to window.matchMedia changes. Returns whether the given media query matches. Always returns false on first render for SSR compatibility.
items.author: Astryx

items.name: hook-use-menu-press
items.title: useMenuPress
items.description: The press model of macOS and iOS menus, for any pointer: the row under the pointer when it is RELEASED is the row that acts, the highlight follows the pointer while it is held, a mouse opens the menu on press and can drag straight into it, and a finger held on the trigger opens it with the finger still down. The pointer is tracked at document level by pointerId, so a finger that slid off the row it landed on is still followed; the click the browser reports at the end of a touch, aimed at the row where the touch began, is swallowed so nothing acts twice. DropdownMenu, ContextMenu, DropdownMenuSubMenu, Selector and the menu bottom sheet already mount it; reach for it directly only when building a menu-like surface of your own.
items.author: Astryx

items.name: hook-use-merged-refs
items.title: useMergedRefs
items.description: Combines multiple object or callback refs into one stable callback ref. Use it when a component must forward a consumer ref while also attaching internal refs. Unlike calling mergeRefs during render, the callback identity stays stable across unrelated rerenders, so React does not detach and reattach the element.
items.author: Astryx

items.name: hook-use-multi-combobox
items.title: useMultiCombobox
items.description: Tracks the active option of a multi-select combobox and handles its keys, while DOM focus stays on the control. It powers MultiSelector; unlike useCombobox, toggling an option keeps the list open, and rows can carry an action cell. It renders nothing and sets no attributes: the caller renders the control and the list, and wires the ARIA attributes from what it returns.
items.author: Astryx

items.name: hook-use-overflow
items.title: useOverflow
items.description: Measures children rendered in a hidden container to determine how many fit in the available width without flickering. Uses ResizeObserver to react to container and measured-child size changes. The measurement container should hold all items plus an optional overflow indicator element (identified by a data-overflow-indicator attribute).
items.author: Astryx

items.name: hook-use-popover
items.title: usePopover
items.description: Headless hook for click-triggered popovers with focus trapping. Combines useLayer with useFocusTrap, auto-focus, light dismiss, Escape handling, and an optional hidden close button for accessible dialog-like popover behavior. Every painted surface emits the canonical popover target. A custom composition needing a distinct stable seam should pass and document its own surfaceTarget.
items.author: Astryx

items.name: hook-use-press-feedback
items.title: usePressFeedback
items.description: The touch press model every Astryx pressable uses, for a local component that paints its own press. Under a finger, CSS `:active` paints on the touch itself and can outlive the start of a scroll; the press model instead waits 150 ms before believing a press, cancels it the moment the finger travels 10 px or a scroll claims the gesture, never brings it back inside that gesture, answers a quick tap at the lift, and fades the release over 200 ms — the clocks a native list uses. One document-level controller does this for every marked element (installed by the first pressable to mount, removed by the last to unmount), so calling the hook adds no listener or state to your element. Under a mouse nothing changes: keep your `:active` rule, and drop it under `@media (pointer: coarse)` the way the built-in components do.
items.author: Astryx

items.name: hook-use-resizable
items.title: useResizable
items.description: Hook for adding drag-to-resize behavior to layout regions. Supports single-region and multi-region configurations with snap points, collapsible panels, localStorage persistence, and cascade resize ordering.
items.author: Astryx

items.name: hook-use-scroll-lock
items.title: useScrollLock
items.description: Locks body scroll when active by pinning the body with position: fixed. This prevents background scrolling behind modals and dialogs, which is necessary for iOS Safari where overscroll-behavior: contain does not work. Restores the original scroll position when unlocked. Pinning hides the document scrollbar, so where that scrollbar takes layout space (desktop) the hook holds its gutter open with scrollbar-gutter: stable for the duration of the lock. The page, including any position: fixed chrome, does not shift sideways.
items.author: Astryx

items.name: hook-use-scroll-overflow
items.title: useScrollOverflow
items.description: Tracks scroll overflow state for a horizontally scrollable container. Returns a ref callback and state booleans that update as the user scrolls or the container resizes. Uses scroll event listeners and ResizeObserver for reactive updates. Tolerance of 1px is applied to avoid sub-pixel false positives.
items.author: Astryx

items.name: hook-use-scrollable-area
items.title: useScrollableArea
items.description: Adds canonical axis-aware scroll behavior to structure owned by the caller. An axis is effective only when its computed overflow is scroll-capable and geometry exceeds the shared 1px tolerance. Both viewport and content boxes are observed.
items.author: Astryx

items.name: hook-use-streaming-text
items.title: useStreamingText
items.description: Smooths bursty streamed text into a steady character-by-character reveal using requestAnimationFrame. Decouples arrival rate from display rate. Advances on word and syntax boundaries to avoid slicing mid-markdown or mid-word, preventing visual glitches with markdown renderers. Animation timing derives from Astryx motion tokens via useTheme when available, with sensible fallbacks outside a theme provider. Snaps to full text when isStreaming becomes false.
items.author: Astryx

items.name: hook-use-table-column-resize
items.title: useTableColumnResize
items.description: Hook that returns a TablePlugin adding draggable resize handles to column header borders. Supports pointer + keyboard (WAI-ARIA window splitter) resizing, RTL, per-column min/max widths, and proportional-column preservation (resizes the neighbor so the table stays full-width). Commits widths on release.
items.author: Astryx

items.name: hook-use-table-column-settings
items.title: useTableColumnSettings
items.description: Headless column visibility and ordering management for Table. Provides filtered columns, toggle helpers, and pre-built MultiSelector options for a column picker UI.
items.author: Astryx

items.name: hook-use-table-filter-state
items.title: useTableFilterState
items.description: Managed state hook for table filtering. Returns the current filter map and an onChange handler. Pass the result directly to useTableFiltering.
items.author: Astryx

items.name: hook-use-table-filtering
items.title: useTableFiltering
items.description: Table plugin that adds inline column filters with popover or inline controls. Pairs with useTableFilterState for managed state. Supports text, select, multi-select, date, and number filter types via PowerSearch field definitions.
items.author: Astryx

items.name: hook-use-table-grouped-rows
items.title: useTableGroupedRows
items.description: Hook that groups a flat data array into collapsible section rows. Each distinct groupBy value becomes a full-width section-header row with a chevron toggle, the group label, and a member count; collapsing hides that group's data rows while keeping the header visible. The disclosure state lives on the chevron button, not the native table row. Mirrors useTableTreeState: the consumer owns the collapsedGroups set and the hook returns {data, plugin, idKey}: pass them to Table as data, plugins, and idKey respectively. Grouping runs on the rows you hand it, so with pagination the order is filter, sort, slice, then group: sort by the group key first and the user's keys second, so a section's rows stay contiguous and each page appends to the bottom of the table instead of splicing rows in above the reader. A page that ends on a row count still cuts mid-section, and the heading then counts what has loaded rather than what exists: "6" quietly becoming "10". Where the full result set is in hand, carry the cut forward to the end of the section it lands in: every rendered section is then whole and its count is a total.
items.author: Astryx

items.name: hook-use-table-pagination
items.title: useTablePagination
items.description: Headless pagination plugin for Table. Call with a config object: `useTablePagination({ page, onPageChange, totalItems })`. Returns a TablePlugin to pass to `<Table plugins={{ pagination: paginationPlugin }} />`.
items.author: Astryx

items.name: hook-use-table-row-expansion
items.title: useTableRowExpansion
items.description: Hook that returns a TablePlugin which expands a full-width detail panel below a row, rendered by the consumer via renderExpanded(item). Adds a leading chevron column and a right-click "Expand/Collapse row" action; the consumer owns the expandedKeys set. The panel spans the row but starts its content at the first column, past the chevron, so detail lines up with the labels above it; the inset follows the table density. Use it for master-detail rows (order details, forms, charts, nested tables). For hierarchical data where child rows reuse the parent columns, use useTableTreeData + useTableTreeState instead.
items.author: Astryx

items.name: hook-use-table-row-index
items.title: useTableRowIndex
items.description: Hook that returns a TablePlugin which prepends a right-aligned, monospaced row-number column. Numbering follows the rendered data order (reflecting the current sort / filter / pagination view) and starts at 1 by default. Astryx renderCell receives only the row item, so the plugin takes the rendered data array to derive each ordinal.
items.author: Astryx

items.name: hook-use-table-row-status
items.title: useTableRowStatus
items.description: Hook that returns a TablePlugin which prepends a narrow column signaling per-row status. Return {status, label} for a semantic success, warning, or error: Table resolves the matching glyph and tone through the active theme. Return {color, icon?, label} for a custom marker: every color is paint-only, an omitted icon renders the stable 8px dot, and an explicit icon renders that caller-selected glyph. Named custom icons keep their released Icon color mapping; raw CSS custom icons inherit the caller's exact paint instead of the previous primary fallback. Existing callers require no source migration. label is required and becomes the accessible image name plus supplemental hover tooltip; return null for no indicator. The column header is visually blank but carries a screen-reader-only localized name ("Row status", i18n key @astryx.table.rowStatus.columnHeader). Memoize getStatus with useCallback for a stable plugin identity.
items.author: Astryx

items.name: hook-use-table-selection
items.title: useTableSelection
items.description: Hook that returns a TablePlugin implementing row selection with checkboxes, select-all, and aria-selected. Uses React Context for independent checkbox re-renders.
items.author: Astryx

items.name: hook-use-table-selection-state
items.title: useTableSelectionState
items.description: State management companion for useTableSelection. Returns selectionConfig for the behaviour plugin plus selectionState for selection-aware UI such as TableSelectionToolbar. Handles disabled/selectable row filtering for select-all automatically: disabled rows are frozen (preserved across select-all/deselect-all), non-selectable rows are excluded.
items.author: Astryx

items.name: hook-use-table-sortable
items.title: useTableSortable
items.description: Headless multi-sort plugin for Table. Call with a config object: `useTableSortable({ sort, onSortChange })`. Returns a TablePlugin to pass to `<Table plugins={{ sort: sortPlugin }} />`.
items.author: Astryx

items.name: hook-use-table-sticky-columns
items.title: useTableStickyColumns
items.description: Hook that returns a TablePlugin which pins a contiguous run of columns to the start and/or end edge of the table. Pinned columns get cumulative offsets and a soft, scroll-aware shadow over the scrolling content. An empty config ({}) is a valid no-op that pins nothing.
items.author: Astryx

items.name: hook-use-table-tree-data
items.title: useTableTreeData
items.description: Headless tree plugin for Table: renders nested rows with per-level indentation and expand/collapse chevrons in the tree column (the first column by default), and reflects hierarchy on body rows via aria-level and aria-expanded. Composable with the other Table plugins: the canonical plugin order places tree before selection, so the checkbox column lands left of the indented tree column. Feed it the treeConfig from useTableTreeState, or construct the config directly for server-driven or pre-flattened trees. When no row is expandable (flat data), every transform is a pass-through and the table renders identically to one without the plugin. Known limitation: the tree column wraps its cell content, so textOverflow="truncate" tooltips do not apply within the tree column.
items.author: Astryx

items.name: hook-use-table-tree-state
items.title: useTableTreeState
items.description: State management companion for useTableTreeData. Owns the expanded set (controlled or uncontrolled) and flattens nested data into the visible row array; collapsed subtrees are unmounted, not hidden, so the table body contains exactly the visible rows. Returns expandAll/collapseAll helpers, the aggregate isAllExpanded state (true/false/indeterminate) for a header expand-all control, and a ready-to-use config for the tree plugin. Note: because collapsed rows unmount, cell-local React state inside collapsed subtrees is lost on collapse; lift state that must survive.
items.author: Astryx

items.name: hook-use-theme
items.title: useTheme
items.description: Programmatic access to theme tokens for non-CSS consumers like SVG, canvas, Vega, D3, maps, or chart libraries that need values in JavaScript instead of CSS custom property references.
items.author: Astryx

items.name: hook-use-toast
items.title: useToast
items.description: Hook for showing toast notifications from anywhere in your component tree. Returns a function that accepts toast options and shows the notification. Works automatically with LayerProvider or self-mounts a fallback viewport.
items.author: Astryx

items.name: hook-use-tooltip
items.title: useTooltip
items.description: Headless hook for hover/focus-triggered tooltips. Builds on useLayer with hover intent, keyboard focus handling, and accessible aria-describedby linking. Use for custom trigger elements that need tooltip behavior without the wrapper component.
items.author: Astryx

items.name: hook-use-translator
items.title: useTranslator
items.description: Returns a translator function that resolves keys against the current locale, provider overrides, and the shipped English fallback catalog. Call inside a component; the returned function can be used anywhere within that component's scope.
items.author: Astryx

items.name: hook-use-tree-focus
items.title: useTreeFocus
items.description: Manages roving-tabindex focus and the WAI-ARIA tree keyboard model. ArrowUp/ArrowDown/Home/End roam linearly over the visible treeitems (skipping disabled ones), while ArrowRight/ArrowLeft carry tree semantics (expand/collapse, move to first-child/parent). Enter/Space activate, and printable characters trigger typeahead.
items.author: Astryx

items.name: hook-use-typeahead
items.title: useTypeahead
items.description: Adds APG type-to-focus search to a collection: printable keystrokes are buffered (resetting after a pause), and the first item whose label starts with the buffer is reported through onMatch. Pressing the same letter repeatedly cycles through the matches rather than filtering deeper. It moves nothing itself; pair it with the collection's own focus management, most often useListFocus or useGridFocus.
items.author: Astryx

items.name: example-banner-dismiss

items.description: Let the user close a banner after reading it. Use for maintenance notices, feature tips, or any non-critical message the user can acknowledge.
items.author: Astryx

items.name: example-banner-floating
items.title: Banner — Floating
items.description: A floating banner raised with `elevation="med"`. Banners are inline by default; raise one when it should read as an overlay above content.
items.author: Astryx

items.name: example-banner-full-width
items.title: Banner — Full Width
items.description: A full-width banner with no border radius for page-level notifications. Use at the top of a page for site-wide announcements or maintenance alerts.
items.author: Astryx

items.name: example-banner-statuses
items.title: Banner — Statuses
items.description: All 4 banner statuses: info, success, warning, and error. Use to show persistent messages like updates, confirmations, cautions, or problems at the top of a page or section.
items.author: Astryx

items.name: example-base-typeahead-custom-search-bar
items.title: Base Typeahead
items.description: A custom result renderer that adds supporting metadata while BaseTypeahead retains option semantics and keyboard behavior.
items.author: Astryx

items.name: example-blockquote-testimonials
items.title: Blockquote — Testimonials
items.description: Multiple quotes arranged in a card grid for a testimonials section. Combine with Card and Grid to create social-proof layouts.
items.author: Astryx

items.name: example-blockquote-with-attribution
items.title: Blockquote — With Attribution
items.description: A plain quote and a quote with a cite attribution. Use cite to credit the original author or source.
items.author: Astryx

items.name: example-bottom-sheet-height-variants
items.title: Bottom Sheet — Height variants
items.description: Compares hug, capped, and tall starting heights for different amounts of content.
items.author: Astryx

items.name: example-bottom-sheet-mobile-keyboard
items.title: Bottom Sheet — Mobile keyboard
items.description: Uses a tall, scrollable form that keeps focused controls visible above the mobile keyboard.
items.author: Astryx

items.name: example-bottom-sheet-no-scrim
items.title: Bottom Sheet — No scrim
items.description: Keeps the page visible and interactive behind a non-modal bottom sheet.
items.author: Astryx

items.name: example-bottom-sheet-snap-points
items.title: Bottom Sheet — Snap points
items.description: Drag-to-resize stops: a half-height working surface, and a peek that slides away and thins the scrim.
items.author: Astryx

items.name: example-bottom-sheet-switcher-review-flow
items.title: Bottom Sheet Switcher — Review flow
items.description: A two-step form flow that lets a person review settings, confirm them, or move back, each step in its own native dialog under one scrim.
items.author: Astryx

items.name: example-breadcrumb-item-basic
items.title: BreadcrumbItem — Basic
items.description: Breadcrumb links inside a Breadcrumbs trail. Ancestor pages get an href; mark the last item with isCurrent to render it as plain text for the current page.
items.author: Astryx

items.name: example-breadcrumbs-deep-path
items.title: Breadcrumbs — Deep Path
items.description: A 5-level breadcrumb trail for deeply nested content. Use in e-commerce, file browsers, or any UI with several levels of hierarchy.
items.author: Astryx

items.name: example-breadcrumbs-icons
items.title: Breadcrumbs — Icons
items.description: Add icons before breadcrumb labels for quick recognition. Use a home icon on the root item and contextual icons on key sections.
items.author: Astryx

items.name: example-breadcrumbs-menu-item
items.title: Breadcrumbs — Menu item
items.description: Give a mid-trail crumb a `menu` prop to turn it into a menu trigger for switching between sibling destinations. It reuses the same item API as DropdownMenu, so an existing option array (or composed item children) drops in verbatim.
items.author: Astryx

items.name: example-breadcrumbs-separators
items.title: Breadcrumbs — Separators
items.description: Swap the default "/" for a different character like chevrons, arrows, or dots. Use when the visual style of the page calls for a different separator.
items.author: Astryx

items.name: example-breadcrumbs-variants
items.title: Breadcrumbs — Variants
items.description: Compare the default and supporting variants side by side. Use the supporting variant in dense UIs like admin panels where the breadcrumb should be subtle.
items.author: Astryx

items.name: example-button-end-slot
items.title: Button — End Slot
items.description: Buttons with a trailing badge showing a count or status. Use for notification counts, unread messages, or any button that needs a visual indicator.
items.author: Astryx

items.name: example-button-floating
items.title: Button — Floating
items.description: A floating action button raised with `elevation="med"`. Use elevation for buttons that hover above content, like a FAB.
items.author: Astryx

items.name: example-button-group-basic
items.title: ButtonGroup — Basic
items.description: Three related actions joined into a single connected control. Provide a group label for accessibility and keep all buttons the same variant so they read as one unit.
items.author: Astryx

items.name: example-button-group-floating
items.title: ButtonGroup — Floating
items.description: A grouped action bar raised with `elevation="med"`. The connected buttons share one surface, so the shadow lifts them as a unit.
items.author: Astryx

items.name: example-button-icon
items.title: Button — Icon
items.description: Buttons with a leading icon that reinforces the label. Use when the icon helps the user identify the action faster, like a plus for "New" or a trash can for "Delete".
items.author: Astryx

items.name: example-button-sizes
items.title: Button — Sizes
items.description: Small, medium, and large buttons side by side. Use small in dense UIs like toolbars, medium for most cases, and large for prominent CTAs.
items.author: Astryx

items.name: example-button-variants
items.title: Button — Variants
items.description: All 4 button variants in default, disabled, and loading states. Use primary for the main action, secondary for most others, ghost for low-emphasis, and destructive for dangerous actions.
items.author: Astryx

items.name: example-calendar-constraints
items.title: Calendar — Constraints
items.description: Limit which dates can be selected using min/max bounds and custom rules like weekdays only. Use for scheduling UIs where certain dates are unavailable.
items.author: Astryx

items.name: example-calendar-range
items.title: Calendar — Range
items.description: Pick a start and end date with the range highlighted between them. Use for booking dates, time-off requests, or report filters.
items.author: Astryx

items.name: example-calendar-single
items.title: Calendar — Single
items.description: Pick one date from a month grid. Use for appointment dates, due dates, or any field that needs a single date.
items.author: Astryx

items.name: example-calendar-two-months
items.title: Calendar — Two Months
items.description: Two months side by side for selecting ranges that span a month boundary. Use in booking or travel UIs where check-in and check-out often fall in different months.
items.author: Astryx

items.name: example-card-callout
items.title: Card — Callout
items.description: Muted-variant cards for tips, notes, or supplementary information. Use when content should be visually distinct but not prominent. The muted variant uses a wash background instead of the elevated default, making it feel recessed rather than raised. Works well in sidebars, help panels, or inline callouts.
items.author: Astryx

items.name: example-card-elevations
items.title: Card — Elevations
items.description: The four elevation levels side by side. Cards are flat by default; raise a card with `elevation` only when it needs to float above surrounding content.
items.author: Astryx

items.name: example-card-layout
items.title: Card — Layout
items.description: A card with a structured header, content area, and footer with action buttons. Use for forms, dialogs, or settings panels that need clear sections. Pair Card with Layout to get automatic dividers between header, content, and footer. The footer aligns actions to the right by default.
items.author: Astryx

items.name: example-card-simple
items.title: Card — Simple
items.description: A card with a heading and body text. Use for summaries, descriptions, or any grouped content that needs visual separation from the page. The card handles its own border, background, and padding; just pass your content as children. Set a width to constrain it, or leave it to fill the parent.
items.author: Astryx

items.name: example-card-variants
items.title: Card — Variants
items.description: Default, muted, and color variants side by side. Use color variants to categorize cards visually, like team colors, project tags, or content types. Each color uses the corresponding background token from the theme, so they adapt to light and dark mode automatically.
items.author: Astryx

items.name: example-carousel-cards
items.title: Carousel — Cards
items.description: A horizontally scrollable row of cards with snap scrolling enabled. Use for feature grids, product lists, or any set of cards that overflows the available width. The carousel adds fade edges and navigation buttons automatically.
items.author: Astryx

items.name: example-carousel-snap
items.title: Carousel — Snap
items.description: Scroll-snap carousel with navigation buttons and team member cards. Each card snaps to the start edge on scroll. Use when items should be viewed one at a time rather than as a continuous strip.
items.author: Astryx

items.name: example-center-horizontal-center
items.title: Center — Horizontal Center
items.description: A formatting control group centered with axis="horizontal" in the default horizontal writing mode. In other writing modes, Center currently follows the flex main axis rather than guaranteeing physical horizontal centering.
items.author: Astryx

items.name: example-center-vertical-horizontal-center
items.title: Center — Vertical & Horizontal Center
items.description: An empty state with an icon, heading, and description centered both vertically and horizontally inside a card. This is the most common use of Center: placing content in the middle of a fixed-height area like a panel, card, or content region. The height prop defines the centering space.
items.author: Astryx

items.name: example-chat-composer-attachments
items.title: ChatComposer — Attachments
items.description: Chat composer with removable file tokens in a collapsible drawer. Use when users can attach files or context to their message.
items.author: Astryx

items.name: example-chat-composer-drawer-feedback
items.title: ChatComposerDrawer — Feedback
items.description: Chat composer drawer with a feedback prompt and selectable lettered options. Use for user confirmation workflows that require explicit action before proceeding.
items.author: Astryx

items.name: example-chat-composer-flat
items.title: ChatComposer — Flat
items.description: The composer is raised by default (`elevation="low"`). Set `elevation="none"` to flatten it; it then draws a border with the same rest / hover / focus treatment as a text input.
items.author: Astryx

items.name: example-chat-composer-footer-actions
items.title: ChatComposer — Footer Actions
items.description: Chat composer with dropdown menus for a model selector and settings in the footer, and a mic button in the send actions slot.
items.author: Astryx

items.name: example-chat-composer-full-featured
items.title: ChatComposer — Full Featured
items.description: Chat composer with all slots populated: collapsible attachment drawer, header actions, context progress bar, footer dropdown menus, and mic button. Shows the maximum composer configuration.
items.author: Astryx

items.name: example-chat-composer-input-controlled
items.title: ChatComposerInput — Controlled
items.description: Controlled chat input with live value display. Use controlled mode when you need to read or transform the input value outside the composer.
items.author: Astryx

items.name: example-chat-composer-input-disabled
items.title: ChatComposerInput — Disabled
items.description: Composer in a disabled state. Use when the input should be visible but not interactive, such as during streaming or when a prerequisite is unmet.
items.author: Astryx

items.name: example-chat-composer-input-mentions
items.title: ChatComposerInput — Mentions
items.description: Chat input with an @ trigger that opens a typeahead menu for mentioning users. Selected names appear as inline tokens.
items.author: Astryx

items.name: example-chat-composer-input-multiple-triggers
items.title: ChatComposerInput — Multiple Triggers
items.description: Chat input with both @ mentions and / commands. Each trigger type renders tokens in a distinct color so users can tell them apart at a glance.
items.author: Astryx

items.name: example-chat-composer-input-slash-commands
items.title: ChatComposerInput — Slash Commands
items.description: Chat input with a / trigger for command selection. Use for AI assistants or bots that support structured commands.
items.author: Astryx

items.name: example-chat-composer-simple
items.title: ChatComposer — Simple
items.description: Minimal chat composer with a placeholder and submit handler. The simplest way to drop a message input into a page.
items.author: Astryx

items.name: example-chat-composer-streaming
items.title: ChatComposer — Streaming
items.description: Chat composer with streaming state and a stop button. Use when the assistant is generating a response and the user can cancel.
items.author: Astryx

items.name: example-chat-composer-validation
items.title: ChatComposer — Validation
items.description: Chat composer with error and warning status messages. Status can appear above or below the composer to surface validation or system feedback.
items.author: Astryx

items.name: example-chat-tool-calls-expandable
items.title: ChatToolCalls — Expandable
items.description: Tool calls with expandable result details showing diffs and command output in code blocks. Click a row to reveal its result.
items.author: Astryx

items.name: example-chat-tool-calls-simple
items.title: ChatToolCalls — Simple
items.description: A single inline tool call above a collapsible multi-call group with diff stats. Shows both layouts side by side.
items.author: Astryx

items.name: example-chat-tool-calls-statuses
items.title: ChatToolCalls — Statuses
items.description: All four status states (pending, running, complete, and error) shown together in a single group.
items.author: Astryx

items.name: example-checkbox-input-indeterminate
items.title: CheckboxInput — Indeterminate
items.description: A "select all" checkbox that controls a group of options. When only some options are checked, it shows a dash instead of a checkmark. Clicking it checks or unchecks everything.
items.author: Astryx

items.name: example-checkbox-input-states
items.title: CheckboxInput — States
items.description: Checkboxes with labels and descriptions in checked, unchecked, and disabled states. Each checkbox controls a single on/off setting. Add a description to explain what the setting does.
items.author: Astryx

items.name: example-checkbox-input-status
items.title: CheckboxInput — Status
items.description: Checkboxes with error, warning, and success validation messages. Use the status prop to show feedback after form validation: errors block submission, warnings inform, and success confirms.
items.author: Astryx

items.name: example-checkbox-list-item-basic
items.title: CheckboxListItem — Basic
items.description: Checkbox items with labels and descriptions inside a controlled CheckboxList. Use for multi-select option groups like notification preferences.
items.author: Astryx

items.name: example-checkbox-list-select-all-with-indeterminate
items.title: CheckboxList — Select All With Indeterminate
items.description: A "select all" toggle at the top of a checkbox list that switches to an indeterminate dash when only some items are checked, useful for bulk actions like exporting documents or assigning permissions where users often want everything at once.
items.author: Astryx

items.name: example-checkbox-list-with-end-content
items.title: CheckboxList — With End Content
items.description: Badges in the trailing slot show contextual info, like a price or status, next to each option without cluttering the label, so users can compare choices at a glance.
items.author: Astryx

items.name: example-citation-inline-text
items.title: Citation — Inline Text
items.description: Citations embedded within a paragraph of text, showing how they flow inline with surrounding content.
items.author: Astryx

items.name: example-citation-source-list
items.title: Citation — Source List
items.description: A list of citation sources with icons, as you might show at the end of an AI-generated response or article footer.
items.author: Astryx

items.name: example-clickable-card-elevated
items.title: Clickable Card — Elevated
items.description: A clickable card raised with `elevation="med"` so the shadow signals the whole surface is interactive.
items.author: Astryx

items.name: example-clickable-card-with-nested-button
items.title: Clickable Card — Nested Button
items.description: A product card that navigates on click but has an independent "Add to cart" button inside.
items.author: Astryx

items.name: example-code-block-code-config
items.title: Code — Config
items.description: A JSON configuration file with a title bar and line numbers. The title prop adds a filename label in the header so readers know which file the code belongs to.
items.author: Astryx

items.name: example-code-block-code-highlighted
items.title: Code — Highlighted
items.description: TypeScript code with specific lines highlighted to draw attention to a key section. Use highlightLines to call out new or important code in tutorials and changelogs.
items.author: Astryx

items.name: example-code-block-code-scrollable
items.title: Code — Scrollable
items.description: A long code block with a max height that enables vertical scrolling. Use maxHeight to keep the block from dominating the page when displaying large files.
items.author: Astryx

items.name: example-code-block-code-snippet
items.title: Code — Snippet
items.description: Short terminal commands with a copy button and no line numbers. Use for install instructions or one-liner commands that readers will paste directly.
items.author: Astryx

items.name: example-code-block-code-terminal
items.title: Code — Terminal
items.description: A dark terminal-style command block: a bash CodeBlock wrapped in SyntaxTheme with the GitHub Dark preset, copy button on, and no line numbers. Use for shell sessions or CLI output that should read as a terminal even on light pages. Reach for a dark syntax preset instead of hand-rolling a dark box with custom CSS.
items.author: Astryx

items.name: example-code-content-types
items.title: Code — Content Types
items.description: Inline code used for variables, terminal commands, CSS properties, file paths, and keyboard shortcuts. Shows how Code adapts to different kinds of technical content.
items.author: Astryx

items.name: example-code-inline
items.title: Code — Inline
items.description: Inline code references mixed within a paragraph of body text. Use Code to mark up function names, hooks, or API terms so they stand out from surrounding prose.
items.author: Astryx

items.name: example-code-text-sizes
items.title: Code — Text Sizes
items.description: Inline code rendered inside heading, body, supporting, and label text. Code automatically matches the font size of its parent text element.
items.author: Astryx

items.name: example-collapsible-controlled
items.title: Collapsible — Controlled
items.description: Manage the open section from parent state, so something other than a click can move it: a URL parameter, a form jumping to the step that failed validation, or the Previous/Next controls shown here. onChange hands back the whole open value.
items.author: Astryx

items.name: example-collapsible-faq
items.title: Collapsible — FAQ
items.description: FAQ built with hasDividers: row hairlines and density padding with no custom CSS. Questions set their own type — body at semibold, not the trigger's default 17px large — so a list of questions reads as rows rather than a stack of headings, and question and answer separate on weight and color instead of size.
items.author: Astryx

items.name: example-collapsible-group-density
items.title: CollapsibleGroup — Density
items.description: density sets the block padding on every row in the group, so a list of sections can be tuned to the surface it sits on without touching the rows. compact for dense surfaces like sidebars and inspectors, balanced (the default) for page content, spacious for a short list that is the main thing on the page. It follows Table's scale and pairs with hasDividers, which turns it on at balanced.
items.author: Astryx

items.name: example-collapsible-multiple-mode
items.title: Collapsible — Multiple Mode
items.description: Several sections open at once, for comparing across them — feature lists, pricing tiers. One Collapsible per Card, so each trigger keeps its own large type: it is the heading of its surface, not a row in a list.
items.author: Astryx

items.name: example-collapsible-single-mode
items.title: Collapsible — Single Mode
items.description: Only one section open at a time, so a single body of content competes for attention. Use defaultValue to pre-expand whichever section a first-time reader needs. Each Collapsible owns a Section, so its trigger is that section heading.
items.author: Astryx

items.name: example-collapsible-with-dividers
items.title: Collapsible — With Dividers
items.description: A flat list on the page background with hand-placed Dividers, for detail panels and sidebars where cards would add too much weight. Rows, so the triggers step down to body-semibold and a supporting metadata line sits under each answer.
items.author: Astryx

items.name: example-command-palette-async-search
items.title: CommandPalette — Async Search
items.description: Server-side search with loading spinner and custom empty states.
items.author: Astryx

items.name: example-command-palette-custom-footer
items.title: CommandPalette — Custom Footer
items.description: Command palette with a custom footer tip message.
items.author: Astryx

items.name: example-command-palette-empty-basic
items.title: CommandPaletteEmpty — Basic
items.description: A command palette with no results, showing a custom empty message via emptyBootstrapText. Use to explain why the palette is empty and what the user can do next.
items.author: Astryx

items.name: example-command-palette-footer-basic
items.title: CommandPaletteFooter — Basic
items.description: A command palette footer with no children, rendering the built-in keyboard navigation hints. Use CommandPaletteFooter without content to get the default arrow-key, Enter, and Esc hints below the results list.
items.author: Astryx

items.name: example-command-palette-group-basic
items.title: CommandPaletteGroup — Basic
items.description: Command palette items organized under group headings using the composed CommandPaletteGroup form. Use to separate related commands into labeled sections.
items.author: Astryx

items.name: example-command-palette-grouped
items.title: CommandPalette — Grouped
items.description: Command palette with items grouped via auxiliaryData.group.
items.author: Astryx

items.name: example-command-palette-input-with-end-content
items.title: CommandPaletteInput — With End Content
items.description: Custom placeholder and a keyboard shortcut badge in the trailing slot via endContent.
items.author: Astryx

items.name: example-command-palette-item-basic
items.title: CommandPaletteItem — Basic
items.description: Selectable command palette items inside a CommandPaletteList, including highlighted and disabled states. Use when composing a palette manually instead of a search source.
items.author: Astryx

items.name: example-command-palette-list-item-states
items.title: CommandPaletteList — Item States
items.description: Flat list showing the highlighted, selected, and disabled item states. Use CommandPaletteGroup to add section headings.
items.author: Astryx

items.name: example-command-palette-picker-mode
items.title: CommandPalette — Picker Mode
items.description: Single-value picker with persistent selection and check indicator.
items.author: Astryx

items.name: example-command-palette-rich-items
items.title: CommandPalette — Rich Items
items.description: Custom item rendering with icons, keyboard shortcuts, and keyword search.
items.author: Astryx

items.name: example-complex-selector-deadline-picker
items.title: Complex Selector — Deadline Picker
items.description: A multi-step deadline field: pick a preset like Today or Next week, or switch to a custom date and time before applying. The popup stays open until the user commits, so the content owns the Apply action.
items.author: Astryx

items.name: example-complex-selector-tree-search
items.title: Complex Selector — Tree Search
items.description: A destination picker that combines a search field with a TreeList hierarchy. TreeList owns tree keyboard navigation; ComplexSelector owns the trigger, popover, and focus restore. Selecting a folder closes the popup.
items.author: Astryx

items.name: example-context-menu-basic
items.title: ContextMenu — Basic
items.description: An adaptive context area: long-press opens a BottomSheet on compact touch screens, while right-click opens a cursor-positioned menu elsewhere.
items.author: Astryx

items.name: example-context-menu-bottom-sheet
items.title: ContextMenu — Bottom Sheet
items.description: A ContextMenu using the explicit BottomSheet presentation. Long-press the target on touch devices or right-click it with a pointer. Keep a visible menu trigger for important mobile actions.
items.author: Astryx

items.name: example-context-menu-item-basic
items.title: ContextMenuItem — Basic
items.description: Context menu items with labels and secondary descriptions. Use ContextMenuItem to render custom menu entries with consistent styling.
items.author: Astryx

items.name: example-date-input-clearable
items.title: DateInput — Clearable
items.description: Date input with a clear button that resets the value. Use when the date field is optional and the user may need to undo their selection.
items.author: Astryx

items.name: example-date-input-description
items.title: DateInput — Description
items.description: Date input with helper text below the label explaining what the field expects. Use when the purpose of the date is not obvious from the label alone.
items.author: Astryx

items.name: example-date-input-formats
items.title: DateInput — Formats
items.description: The format prop reuses Timestamp's format vocabulary to control how the committed value is displayed: date, date_long (default), date_weekday, and system_date, or a function for a fully custom string. Formatting applies only to the committed value, never to text the user is actively typing.
items.author: Astryx

items.name: example-date-input-min-max-constraints
items.title: DateInput — Min/Max Constraints
items.description: Date input constrained to a min/max window. Use when only certain dates are valid, like booking availability or a fiscal quarter.
items.author: Astryx

items.name: example-date-input-validation
items.title: DateInput — Validation
items.description: Date input in all three status states: error, warning, and success. Use to surface validation issues, caution the user, or confirm a valid selection.
items.author: Astryx

items.name: example-date-range-input-validation
items.title: DateRangeInput — Validation
items.description: Date range input in all three status states: error, warning, and success. Use to surface booking conflicts, flag high-demand periods, or confirm an available range.
items.author: Astryx

items.name: example-date-range-input-with-presets
items.title: DateRangeInput — With Presets
items.description: Date range picker with quick-select presets for common periods. Use for analytics dashboards, report filters, or any context where users frequently select standard time windows.
items.author: Astryx

items.name: example-date-time-input-validation
items.title: DateTimeInput — Validation
items.description: DateTimeInput in all three status states: error, warning, and success. Use to surface scheduling conflicts, caution the user about edge cases, or confirm a valid datetime.
items.author: Astryx

items.name: example-dialog-adaptive-presentation
items.title: Dialog — Adaptive presentation
items.description: Opt-in recipe for an AdaptiveDialog wrapper: Dialog remains the default everywhere, while touchPresentation="bottom-sheet" switches only at lg and below when pointer is coarse and hover is unavailable. Includes a deterministic presentation override for tests/unusual environments and notes that BottomSheet purpose controls swipe and scrim dismissal. Usage examples: touchPresentation="dialog" keeps Dialog, "fullscreen" chooses fullscreen Dialog, and "bottom-sheet" chooses BottomSheet only for the touch-oriented range. Keep presentation as the deterministic override. Do not use this by default for AlertDialog or destructive confirmations.
items.author: Astryx

items.name: example-dialog-confirmation
items.title: Dialog — Confirmation
items.description: Asks the user to confirm a destructive action before it happens. Use before deleting projects, removing team members, revoking API keys, or any irreversible operation.
items.author: Astryx

items.name: example-dialog-form
items.title: Dialog — Form
items.description: Collects user input without navigating away from the page. Uses purpose="form" so clicking the backdrop won't close it. Use for editing profiles, creating items, or updating settings inline.
items.author: Astryx

items.name: example-dialog-fullscreen
items.title: Dialog — Fullscreen
items.description: Takes over the entire viewport for content that needs maximum space. Use for documentation viewers, rich text editors, multi-step wizards, or media previews where the standard dialog width is too narrow.
items.author: Astryx

items.name: example-dialog-header-basic
items.title: DialogHeader — Basic
items.description: A DialogHeader with a title, subtitle, and close button, placed in the header slot of a Dialog Layout. Pass onOpenChange to render the close button.
items.author: Astryx

items.name: example-dialog-required
items.title: Dialog — Required
items.description: Cannot be dismissed by Escape or backdrop click; the user must explicitly choose an action. Uses purpose="required". Use for ownership transfers, legal acknowledgements, or critical decisions where skipping is not an option.
items.author: Astryx

items.name: example-dialog-scrollable
items.title: Dialog — Scrollable

Every variant occupies the same 16px box, so a step swapping its number for a check as it completes never shifts the label beside it. The last cell shows that a custom node can be live rather than static: a Spinner on a step that is in progress, shaded `inherit` so it picks up the step's own tint like any other glyph.

items.name: template-form-wizard-dialog

Best for two to four short steps — setup, invite, schedule, onboarding — where losing the context underneath would cost more than the flow is worth.

items.title: Vertical Wizard
items.description: Multi-step wizard with the steps in a fixed left rail that stays visible while the form scrolls, plus a side panel whose guidance follows the focused field. items.name: template-ide
items.title: IDE
items.description: Dense multi-pane workspace of resizable, collapsible regions: a hierarchy tree on one flank, tabbed documents in the middle, a docked drawer along the bottom, an inspector opposite. Drag a divider to resize or collapse any of them.
items.author: Astryx

items.name: template-incident-console
items.title: Incident Console
items.description: Dense row queue with an inspector: severity-coded rows grouped by status, a saved-search filter bar, a segmented status control, and a resizable detail pane for the selected row. Rows, not cards, sized for scanning volume.
items.author: Astryx

items.name: template-kanban-board
items.title: Kanban Board
items.description: Horizontal lanes of draggable cards where the column itself is the status, so drag and drop between lanes is the state change. Fixed columns, variable-height cards.
items.author: Astryx

items.name: template-library
items.title: Card Grid
items.description: Searchable, browsable card grid with filter tabs and a real empty state: uniform tiles organized by topic, narrowing in place, with no detail surface behind them.
items.author: Astryx

items.name: template-login
items.title: Basic Login
items.description: Minimal centered credential form on a plain ground: two fields and a submit, nothing competing for attention. The least-chrome entry surface.
items.author: Astryx

items.name: template-login-card
items.title: Login Card
items.description: Credential form inside an elevated centered card, third-party provider buttons separated from the fields by a divider, secondary sign-up and legal links beneath.
items.author: Astryx

items.name: template-login-split
items.title: Login Split
items.description: Credential form filling one half of a two-pane split, full-bleed media holding the other. Same fields as the card variant, but the layout carries brand imagery.
items.author: Astryx

items.name: template-login-sso
items.title: Login SSO
items.description: Progressive credential flow that branches on input: the email domain resolves an identity provider and redirects, with a password path as fallback. Two-stage rather than one form.
items.author: Astryx

items.name: template-messaging-shell
items.title: Messaging Shell
items.description: Four-column nested navigation narrowing left to right (team workspace, channel list, message stream, thread panel) where each column scopes the next. Dense rows, zero cards.
items.author: Astryx

items.name: template-mixed-gallery
items.title: Mixed Gallery
items.description: Masonry grid of variable-height tiles that pack against each other instead of cropping to a shared ratio, captioned per tile. Irregular rhythm, unlike the uniform gallery.
items.author: Astryx

items.name: template-payment-form
items.title: Checkout Form
items.description: Long sectioned form running beside a summary that stays visible while the fields scroll and recalculates as they change, ending on a terminal confirm of the total. Sections run contact, address, delivery choice, then card details.
items.author: Astryx

items.name: template-product-detail
items.title: Product Detail
items.description: Single-item detail pairing a media gallery with a selection column: variant swatches, a quantity stepper, primary and secondary commit actions, and collapsible specification sections below.
items.author: Astryx

items.name: template-product-gallery
items.title: Product Gallery
items.description: Uniform card grid where every tile carries media, title, supporting line, and a price. Browse-to-select only, with no filtering and no detail surface.
items.author: Astryx

items.name: template-settings
items.title: Settings Form
items.description: Preferences as one continuously scrolling form, sections stacked in order with no navigation between them. The simplest settings shape: everything reachable by scrolling.
items.author: Astryx

items.name: template-settings-dialog
items.title: Settings Dialog
items.description: Preferences inside a modal container with searchable section navigation, so configuration happens without leaving whatever is underneath. Grouped toggles, live preview of appearance choices, rebindable shortcuts.
items.author: Astryx

items.name: template-settings-sidebar
items.title: Settings Panels
items.description: Preferences split into nav-switched panels: a persistent section list swaps the pane beside it, and rows edit in place rather than opening a separate form.
items.author: Astryx

items.name: template-shell-nav
items.title: Shell Nav
items.description: Application frame combining both navigation axes: a top menu bar with command-palette search over a resizable hierarchy rail, wrapping placeholder content. For when one axis is not enough.
items.author: Astryx

items.name: template-shell-side-nav
items.title: Side Nav
items.description: Application frame with a single collapsible, resizable left rail carrying grouped history and search, wrapping the main content. Vertical navigation only, no top bar.
items.author: Astryx

items.name: template-shell-top-nav
items.title: Top Nav
items.description: Application frame with horizontal navigation only: a centered bar whose items open full-width mega-menu panels, over placeholder content that keeps the entire width.
items.author: Astryx

items.name: template-side-gallery
items.title: Side Gallery
items.description: Asymmetric split section: a copy column of headline, supporting text, and links held against a clustered image collage opposite. Deliberately off-balance, unlike the centered hero.
items.author: Astryx

items.name: template-table
items.title: Simple Table
items.description: Flat row collection where columns sort, rows select into a bulk-action toolbar, and each row carries an overflow menu. Sortable but ungrouped, with no detail pane, the baseline shape.
items.author: Astryx

items.name: template-table-collapsible
items.title: Collapsible Table
items.description: Several tables on one page, each in a collapsible card with its own columns — for groups that do not share a schema, where one table would stand full of empty cells. One time range drives them all, and rows expand into a history chart. Accounts, integrations, sections, sort, expand, or collapse.
items.author: Astryx

items.name: template-table-comparison
items.title: Comparison Table
items.description: Transposed matrix that puts candidates in the columns and criteria in grouped rows, with a pinned label column that survives horizontal scroll, columns you can swap or add, and best-in-row marks you can toggle. Compare, comparison, matrix, spec sheet, feature grid, pricing table, benchmark, frozen column, sticky column, or side-by-side.
items.author: Astryx

items.name: template-table-filter
items.title: Filterable Table
items.description: Flat row collection built around progressive filtering: a token bar that escalates into full query syntax, saved views that persist a filter set, column and grouping options, and a resizable detail pane.
items.author: Astryx

items.name: template-table-grouped
items.title: Grouped Table
items.description: Row collection bundled into collapsible sections with per-group counts, so a long list reads as a handful of blocks that expand and collapse. Query filtering and a resizable inspector for the selected row.
items.author: Astryx

items.name: template-table-inbox
items.title: Inbox Table
items.description: Two-pane message queue: the table indexes a reading pane rather than being the destination, with a divider you drag to resize. Rows stack when the table narrows, not the window; threads read as collapsible messages; replying opens a composer that leaves the list live.
items.author: Astryx

items.name: template-table-page
items.title: Searchable Table
items.description: Flat table of uniform rows under a block of record-level facts, narrowed three ways at once — a full-text search box, a scope toggle, and per-column popovers — with sortable and filterable columns, per-row hover detail, and totals derived from the visible rows that flag themselves as partial while a filter is on. The shape for one homogeneous list, not nested rows or groups with their own columns.
items.author: Astryx

items.name: template-table-tree
items.title: Tree Table
items.description: Hierarchical table where every parent row rolls up from its children — a code repository whose folders show the newest commit beneath them, beside a detail sidebar and a rendered README. Columns resize, siblings sort within their own level, arrow keys walk the rows, and search prunes the tree to matching branches.
items.author: Astryx

items.name: template-theme-showcase
items.title: Theme Showcase
items.description: Several unrelated product surfaces rendered together on one canvas so a token change can be judged across contexts at once. A comparison harness rather than a layout to ship.
items.author: Astryx

items.name: template-work-item-detail
items.title: Work Item Detail
items.description: Single work-item detail in two columns: a title with a status selector, a description, a subtask checklist with progress, an attachments block, and a comment and activity feed in the main column, plus a property rail with assignee, dates, labels, and linked items. The shape for any tracked item with children, properties, and a comment history — a task, ticket, issue, story, bug, card, request, or work item.
items.author: Astryx
